newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Infrastructure, EBRD are key for Hungary.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Infrastructure, EBRD are key for Hungary.

text.p: The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) remains committed to help develop infrastructure in Hungary, a key area in the country's race to catch up with the standard of living in the European Union (EU), a senior EBRD official said.

"One of the most important steps in economic transition is the accession to the EU, and one area in bad need of financing is infrastructure," Gyorgy Karady, Director of EBRD's Hungary Team, told Reuters in an interview.

"This (help) could happen via equity investment, underwriting, privatisation through capital markets," he said. EBRD, set up in 1991 with the aim of helping central and east European countries in their transition towards a market economy, has approved projects for Hungary worth over just 1.0 billion Ecu ($1.28 billion) by the end of July.
Of this figure, 300 million Ecu has gone to finance Hungary's transport infrastructure, 273.5 million to telecommunications and 246 million for the financial sector.

Though many commentators believe that the relatively advanced economies of central Europe, Hungary, Poland and the Czech Republic, should be left to stand on their own and that the EBRD should support less developed economies to the east, Karady sees a continued role for the EBRD in Hungary.

"The difference between EBRD and commercial banks is that the latter undertake lending based (on) short banking terms, while the EBRD concentrates on projects with higher risks and on loans with much longer maturities," he said.
He noted that Hungarian companies had shown little appetite for short-term loans of just five-year maturity and needed a longer time span.

"The risk profile of the country and of the companies has changed, and they are not coming to us for loans of five- to seven-years maturity but are looking further out to ten to 15 years. We believe we can undertake this risk," he said.
Hungary's overall risk profile has benefited from an upgrade in its credit rating from Standard & Poor's to BBB-minus rating from BB-plus.
Another area where EBRD sees a role for itself was in acquiring stakes in companies and acting as a partner, rather than just providing loans.
"We are paying increasing attention to capital investments," Karady said.
"It's more and more part of our strategy to finance Hungarian companies with capital and to help companies' privatisation through the bourse as core investor."
The Budapest Stock Exhcange has been among the fastest growing bourses globally this year, but the market has seen only a few new listings in 1996.
"We also help (companies) with underwriting as we did with Borsodchem," Karady said. -- London newsroom + 44 171 542 5887 ($1=.7794 Ecu)
